data.name: Play
data.gender_notes: Play is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.short_meaning: To engage in activity for enjoyment and recreation
data.long_meaning: The act of participating in an activity for enjoyment and recreation. It implies a sense of enjoyment, freedom, and creativity. Play can be a physical activity, such as a game or sport, or a mental activity, such as reading or playing an instrument. The name Play carries the meaning “To engage in activity for enjoyment and recreation” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the English tradition and is also used in English. Parents who choose Play usually hope their child will grow to embody to engage in activity for enjoyment and recreation and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Play represents the childlike wonder and curiosity within us all. It encourages us to explore new things, to take risks, and to find joy in the simple things. Play can also be a form of meditation, allowing us to focus our minds and connect with our inner selves.
data.etymology: Play belongs to the English linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “To engage in activity for enjoyment and recreation.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Play total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: In Hindu culture, play or lila, has a significant place. It's an essential part of life, not just for children but for adults as well. The significance of play can be seen in various aspects of Hinduism, such as in the ancient text, Bhagavad Gita. In the Bhagavad Gita, Shri Krishna advises Arjuna to perform his duties with enthusiasm and devotion, just as a player enjoys the game. The concept of play is also reflected in various Hindu festivals, such as Holi and Diwali, where colorful and joyful activities are indulged in.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, play or lila, is considered a form of devotion and a way to connect with the divine. It symbolizes the ability to transcend the mundane everyday life and enter a realm of creativity, imagination, and untethered joy. Through play, one can access a deeper sense of inner happiness and bliss. Play also highlights the interconnectedness of all aspects of existence, and that even the most seemingly insignificant actions have spiritual significance. Ultimately, play invites us to embrace the fullness of life, to explore our creative potential and to experience the world around us with curiosity and joy.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name "Play" in Hindu tradition symbolizes the free, uninhibited expression of the divine within an individual. It encourages living in the present moment and embracing life's joys and challenges with a light heart and open mind.
